title: Assign per-runner timer and model-provider ownership to the extension that created them, and release them on suspend
wave: Wave 2 — commit 1 (timers) ONLY. Commit 2 (providers + resume) is Wave 4 and is specified here but MUST NOT be implemented in the Wave 2 PR.
one_line: When an extension is disabled, the background intervals it scheduled and the model provider it registered stop taking effect — and both come back when it is enabled again.
user_visible_effect: Disabling an extension in settings now actually stops it. Today a disabled extension that scheduled `ctx.setInterval` keeps polling against the live session forever, and a disabled extension's custom model provider stays in `ModelRegistry` and its API key stays in `authStorage` — so a plugin the user turned off still reaches the network. After this change the interval callback stops firing the moment the extension is suspended, the provider's models disappear from `/model` and its stored key is removed, and re-enabling the extension restores both. Users see this through the existing 'Restart omp to load newly enabled extensions' settings flow: toggling `extensions` / `disabledExtensions` now takes effect for background work and providers instead of only for commands, tools and renderers.
effort: Commit 1: XS — roughly 20-25 changed production lines across 3 existing files, no new files, no public API change. Commit 2: S — a ~2-line new field on the `Extension` interface, a ~4-line fill in one drain block, and a ~6-line insertion in `reconcileExtensionSources`, plus a new test file. Total with the test file: roughly 120 changed lines.
risk: Missing an OWNER ASSIGNMENT POINT, not missing a mechanism. `createContext()` has 15 call sites but only THREE of them can correctly name an owning extension: `#runHandlerWithTimeout` (which already receives `ext`) and the two file-fallback trampolines (which close over `ext`). The other 13 all share one `ctx` built once per emit loop (`ctx ??= this.createContext()` at runner.ts:1478 and :1490), so passing `ext` into `createContext()` at those sites passes `undefined` for every extension and the bug survives on the multi-extension event path — the exact path a real `session_start` / `user_bash` timer takes. A test that only asserts a field was deleted passes on that broken implementation. The second risk, specific to commit 2, is shipping suspend without resume: `pendingProviderRegistrations` is destructively drained (all three consumers assign `[]` back), so a re-call re-registers nothing, turning 'a disabled plugin still connects' into the worse 'I re-enabled the plugin and nothing happens'. That is why the provider half cannot be split from the resume half.

Three assertions. (1) and (3) fail on today's HEAD and go green with the work; (2) passes vacuously on HEAD and only becomes a real gate once commit 1 lands (see plan_corrections #7 — do NOT report it as red-before / green-after).
(1) TIMER DEAD AFTER SUSPEND — an extension schedules `ctx.setInterval` from a `session_start` EVENT handler, is suspended via `setSuspendedExtensions`, and its callback is observed NOT to fire while the session is still alive. The assertion is on the callback counter, never on an internal field being emptied, because a 'fix' that never started the timer also empties the field. Two extensions schedule timers; suspending one must leave the other's still firing.
(2) TIMER ALIVE AFTER RESUME — the same extension is resumed, its handler re-runs, and the newly scheduled callback fires again. This blocks commit 1 being satisfied by a timer that is never started.
(3) PROVIDER GONE AFTER SUSPEND — an extension calls `pi.registerProvider`; after the suspend reconcile the provider name no longer resolves through `ModelRegistry` and `registry.authStorage.keys.source(name)` is `undefined`; after resume both are back.

test_contract.summary: Suspending one extension stops exactly that extension's scheduled callbacks and its registered model provider — no more, no less — and resuming it restores both. The 'no more' half is asserted with two extensions so a shared-context owner bug is caught; the 'no less' half is asserted with a second extension whose timer must keep firing while its neighbour is suspended.
test_contract.what_a_consumer_observes_if_it_regresses: For timers: today a disabled extension's `ctx.setInterval` keeps firing for the life of the session. Nothing throws, nothing is logged — a disabled plugin quietly keeps polling the disk, the network, or an LLM. If the owner is mis-assigned from the shared `ctx`, the failure is a DISABLED-bug that reads like a fix: suspending extension A also kills extension B's healthy timer, and B stays dead even after A is resumed. If the timer is never re-started on the resume path, an extension that polls silently stops polling forever after one disable/enable cycle. For providers: a disabled extension's custom provider keeps resolving through `ModelRegistry`, its stored API key stays in `authStorage.keys`, and `omp models` still lists it — so 'I turned the plugin off' does not remove the credential it was given. If resume is missing, the symmetric failure is worse: re-enabling the plugin restores nothing and the user's provider is simply gone with no error anywhere.

cases.name: TIMER DEAD AFTER SUSPEND, and the sibling extension's timer survives
cases.defends: The single contract 'disabling an extension stops its background work, and only its own'.
cases.how_it_fails_on_HEAD: The callback counter keeps incrementing after suspend. `#timers` is a `Set<Timer>` (managed-timers.ts:23) with no owner, and `setSuspendedExtensions` (runner.ts:947-969) touches only `#suspendedExtensions` and the `extensions` array — nothing reaches the timers.
cases.critical_detail: The handler MUST be registered on a real event (`session_start`) and reached through `runner.emit(...)`, NOT through the file-write / file-delete fallback trampolines. The trampolines only fire when the agent attempts a file mutation, so a test written against them would pass on an implementation that assigns the owner only at runner.ts:779-780 and :798-799 — i.e. it would pass on the exact bug it exists to catch.
asserts: extension A's tick counter is >= 1 before suspend
after `runner.setSuspendedExtensions(ext => ext === A)`, `vi.advanceTimersByTime(5000)` leaves A's counter unchanged while the session is still alive
extension B's counter INCREASED across the same window — a same-tick comparison is not enough; B must demonstrably advance while A does not

cases.name: TIMER ALIVE AFTER RESUME
cases.defends: That clearing on suspend did not become 'clearing forever'. A suspended extension is not unloaded, so the moment it is resumed its handler must be able to schedule managed work again and have it fire.
cases.how_it_fails_if_commit_1_is_wrong: On an implementation that satisfies gate 1 by never scheduling the interval, or by clearing on the resume branch as well as the suspend branch, the counter stays at 0 after resume. Note this case passes vacuously on unmodified HEAD because nothing is ever cleared — see plan_corrections #7.
asserts: after `runner.setSuspendedExtensions(ext => ext === A)` with A no longer matching, emitting the same event again re-runs A's handler
the counter produced by the SECOND handler invocation increases — this is a newly scheduled timer, not the pre-suspend one, and the test must not assert on the old `Timer` handle
the pre-suspend handle is genuinely gone: holding a reference to it and advancing time does not resume the old callback

cases.name: PROVIDER GONE AFTER SUSPEND, and back after RESUME
cases.defends: That a disabled extension contributes no model provider and no stored credential, and that re-enabling it restores both.
cases.how_it_fails_on_HEAD: `reconcileExtensionSources` (sdk.ts:4566-4629) calls only `resetCapabilities()` (:4571) and `setSuspendedExtensions()` (:4579). It never calls `modelRegistry.syncExtensionSources`, so the provider stays registered and the key stays in auth storage.
asserts: after the suspend reconcile, `registry.find(providerName, modelId)` is `undefined`
after the suspend reconcile, `registry.authStorage.keys.source(providerName)` is `undefined` — the credential is removed, not just the model overlay
after the resume reconcile, both are defined again — this is the half that requires the retention record, since `pendingProviderRegistrations` has already been destructively drained

open_questions: RESUME AND TIMERS — the real design decision, and the plan does not answer it. Clearing on suspend is unambiguous. What happens on resume is not: `setSuspendedExtensions`'s resume branch only flips a Set membership, so a resumed extension's background work is gone until its handler next runs. A polling extension therefore stops polling forever after one disable/enable cycle, silently. Three options: (a) accept it and document that a resumed extension re-establishes its own background work on its next event — cheapest, and what this spec's test case 2 assumes; (b) have the resume branch re-emit a synthetic startup event so handlers rebuild their subscriptions — more correct, larger, and arguably belongs to WI-7's lifecycle work; (c) remember cleared timers and re-arm them on resume, which contradicts the whole point of clearing. A human must pick before the code is written. This spec is written for (a) and flags it rather than hiding it.

COMMIT 2 — does the resume re-registration need a `refreshRuntimeProviders()` afterwards? The cold paths in sdk.ts:1010, :2499 and cli/models-cli.ts:364 all call it after registering, and this is the one register site that would not. The counter-argument is that `reconcileExtensionSources` is a settings-listener hot path and `clearSourceRegistrations` already forces a static-model reload. The spec assumes NO refresh (keep the hot path cheap). Confirm or overrule.

COMMIT 2 — `restrictToolNames` asymmetry. The `syncExtensionSources` / `clearSourceRegistrations` pair at sdk.ts:2481-2486 sits inside `if (!restrictToolNames)`, but the retention-record fill at 2487-2492 sits OUTSIDE it. So in a restricted-tool-name session, providers are still registered and still recorded, while the prune never ran. This is pre-existing and out of scope, but the new call in `reconcileExtensionSources` will run in restricted sessions too, which means restricted sessions get a prune they never had. Confirm that is desirable rather than surprising.

COMMIT 2 — should the retention record be cleared if the extension calls `pi.unregisterProvider`? `ExtensionRuntime.unregisterProvider` (loader.ts:108-111) removes an entry from `pendingProviderRegistrations`, which is drained. After the drain it is a no-op. A later resume would re-register a provider the extension explicitly withdrew. Probably rare, but the fix is a line (filter the record on unregister) and it is unclear whether it is worth the surface.

COMMIT 1 — is the `UNOWNED_TIMERS` sentinel from step 6 acceptable, or should `createContext`'s timer helpers throw? A sentinel that silently produces ownerless timers preserves the current behaviour for the trampolines' pre-`#ownTimers` callers and the two existing unit tests. Throwing would surface any future missed owner point immediately but breaks the four existing tests at test/extensions-runner.test.ts:3956-4070 that construct a context directly. The spec recommends the sentinel; a human should ratify it.

plan_corrections.claim: Two constraints on commit 1 that read as design inputs are not.
plan_corrections.verdict: CONFIRMED TRUE — recorded because it is the load-bearing insight
plan_corrections.correction: Both hold exactly as stated, and they are the reason this work item is not a one-liner. (a) `createContext()` has exactly 15 call sites — `grep -n 'this\.createContext(' packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts | wc -l` -> 15 — of which 2 (lines 780, 799) are the file-fallback trampolines that call handlers directly, and 13 share one context across the emit loop via `ctx ??= this.createContext()` (lines 1478 and 1490). Threading `ext` into `createContext()` would pass `undefined` at all 13. (b) `createHandlerContext` (230-241) is `Object.create(ctx)` overriding only `ui`, so the ownerless `setInterval`/`setTimeout` `createContext()` installs at 1304-1305 are inherited by every handler. Both verified, both decisive.

plan_corrections.claim: 'Commit 2 must join the resume record, and the two `createContext` caller shapes mean only three owner points exist' — i.e. the shape of the whole fix.
plan_corrections.verdict: CONFIRMED, with one refinement the plan overstates
plan_corrections.correction: Three owner points is right. The refinement: the plan says the reconcile path 'works in resolvedPath space, so the two spaces must be joined through a mapping that cannot be used directly' (and repeats it under 'where the record lives'). That is true for the `governed`/`enabled` sets at 4577-4578, but it does NOT apply to the provider work. `setSuspendedExtensions` returns `Extension` OBJECTS, and `Extension` carries both `path` and `resolvedPath` — so the source id is a plain `.path` read, and `sourceId` is exactly `extension.path` by construction (loader.ts:363). `extensionRunner.getExtensionPaths()` (927-929) hands over the whole active list in the right key space in one call. No mapping is needed anywhere in the provider half, and building one would be the error.

plan_corrections.claim: Test rows 1-2 fail on HEAD; row 3 also fails on HEAD.
plan_corrections.verdict: PARTLY WRONG — row 2 passes vacuously on HEAD
plan_corrections.correction: Rows 1 and 3 do fail on HEAD. Row 2 (TIMER ALIVE AFTER RESUME) does NOT: on unmodified HEAD nothing is ever cleared, so an interval keeps firing across a suspend/resume cycle and the row passes for the wrong reason. It only becomes a real gate once commit 1 lands — it blocks a commit-1 implementation that satisfies row 1 by never scheduling, or by clearing on the resume branch too. Write it anyway (it is a genuine regression guard), but do not report it as red-before / green-after.
plan_corrections.evidence: managed-timers.ts has no owner concept and setSuspendedExtensions (947-969) touches only `#suspendedExtensions` and the `extensions` array; therefore every scheduled timer keeps running regardless of suspend state at HEAD.
